html:
The state that ruled Morocco in the 1500s and early 1600s under the Saadi dynasty, Arab sharifs who claimed descent from the Prophet. At its height it reached across the Sahara to the Niger.

The Saadis rose in 1510 in the Sous valley in the south, leading the fight against the Portuguese, who held forts on the coast. They took Marrakesh by 1525, won Agadir from Portugal in 1541, and pushed out the Wattasids of Fez by the 1550s. They kept the Ottomans, who held Algiers, out of Morocco.

In 1578 King Sebastian of Portugal invaded and was killed with much of his nobility at the Battle of Ksar el-Kebir, the "Battle of the Three Kings". Portugal soon passed to the Spanish crown. The winner, Ahmad al-Mansur (ruled 1578 to 1603), grew rich on ransoms and sugar and built the El Badi palace in Marrakesh.

In 1590 al-Mansur sent an army with guns across the desert. It beat the Songhai Empire at the Battle of Tondibi in 1591 and took Timbuktu and Gao. The scholar Ahmad Baba was carried off to Marrakesh. After al-Mansur died, his sons fought each other, the state broke apart, and the Alaouite dynasty took over in the 1660s.
sum: The state that ruled Morocco in the 1500s and early 1600s under the Saadi dynasty, Arab sharifs who claimed descent from the Prophet. At its height it reached across the Sahara to the Niger.
